llama.cpp.output: {"answer":"Rain begins when sunlight warms water in oceans, lakes, and rivers. Some water evaporates and rises into the atmosphere as invisible vapor. As the moist air rises, it cools. Cooler air can hold less water vapor, so the vapor condenses onto tiny particles of dust or salt. These small droplets gather to form clouds. Inside a cloud, droplets collide and combine into larger drops. When the drops become too heavy for rising air currents to support, gravity pulls them toward the ground. If the air below the cloud is warm enough, the drops remain liquid and reach the surface as rain."}
